exposure: Opportunistic salpingectomy (OS) at any suitable abdominal surgery
OS only at any suitable gynecologic surgery
OS only at hysterectomy or sterilization
cohort: A simulated population of 1,200,000 million individuals, representing women aged 20-85 years, was used for the analysis.
finding: Interdisciplinary implementation of opportunistic salpingectomy in any suitable abdominal surgeries could contribute to the prevention of ovarian cancer and reduction of healthcare costs, with a broader implementation approach demonstrating substantially better clinical and economic effectiveness.
followup_time: Lifetime (simulated from 20 to 85 years of age)
